I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks on its own (strict mode) and bundles to 206 bytes min+gzip, with 95 bytes of own code. I did not run it against the original on any inputs. lodash isn't installed, so the original `src/module.ts` can't be type-checked or bundled here, and I had nothing to compare against or measure for the own-code allowance.

The installed es-toolkit is 1.53.2, and I read the declarations and sources of the functions below:

- **`byId`:** it uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit` with `(row) => row.id`. It keeps the last element per key, as lodash does. The numeric ids come back as string keys on the object, so the `Record<string, Row>` return type still holds.
- **`totalAge`:** it uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit` with `(row) => row.age`. The non-compat `sumBy` takes only a function, not the `'age'` string shorthand. It sums to 0 for an empty array, matching lodash for these inputs.
- **`dedupeSorted`:** es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. `uniq` returns the same result on sorted integer input, because equal values are adjacent and it keeps the first occurrence in order. I used `uniq` and kept no lodash import. This is the one substitution that relies on the input range (sorted integers) rather than being a drop-in replacement.

I avoided `es-toolkit/compat` because the plain functions cover all three cases and are smaller.

`npx tsc -p .` on the project fails, but only on `src/module.ts`, because it imports lodash. I ran `tsc` directly on `out/module.ts` instead, because `tsconfig.json` includes `src`.
